correctness.rationale: The normalized recurrence period equals the invertible companion-matrix order because a cyclic initial state and its image span the module. Reduction from p² to p gives order h or ph. For distinct characteristic roots, simple-root lifting of X^h−1 determines uniquely their order-preserving lifts and hence their trace and negative norm. For repeated roots, N²=(a²+4b)I/4 and h=pt: when p≥5 the lower-left entry of M^h is nonzero pt λ^{pt−1} mod p²; when p=3 the cubic term cancels precisely at discriminant 6 mod 9. The count of base fibers is elementary. Standalone exact verifier checks all 120894 coefficient lifts for six small odd primes and independent recurrence periods for 2612 of these. These finite tests do not establish the universal proof.

value.rationale: A natural and explicit full census of period-stability over infinitely many prime-square coefficient spaces addresses the parameter-identification gap highlighted in Li (1999). It identifies the unique regular order-preserving lift, proves a uniform obstruction in singular fibers for p≥5, and finds an exceptional 3-adic family; the resulting exact density among all admissible coefficients is (p−1)/p³ for p≥5 and 5/27 at p=3. It does not assert a solution to the fixed-parameter Wall–Sun–Sun problem or higher prime-power classification.
